name: B10-0147/2024 – Motion for a resolution (as a whole)
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the draft Commission implementing decision renewing the authorisation for the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize MON 89034 × 1507 × MON 88017 × 59122 and eight of its sub-combinations pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission to withdraw its plan to renew the licence for a type of genetically modified maize. The maize is engineered to survive spraying with weedkillers and to make its own insect poison. Parliament says the weedkillers involved, including one banned in the EU, are not properly assessed, and that the plan goes beyond the Commission's powers. Parliament also says the licence lacks support from a majority of member states.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament only asks the Commission to withdraw the plan and not authorise such crops.
- **Who it affects:** The Commission, the companies that applied, and farmers and food importers.
- **What happens next:** The Commission decides whether to withdraw or keep the plan; Parliament's request is not binding.
